author: hamzaburney
body:
# Overview
Implemented the initial MVP of a campus‑focused marketplace that enables verified students to list, discover, and securely purchase second‑hand textbooks.

# What was built
## ✅ Student Verification & Registration
- Integrated university email OAuth to confirm student status.
- Added profile onboarding flow with optional profile picture and major selection.
- Stored verification flag in the user schema for permission gating.

## ✅ Listing Creation Wizard
- Multi‑step form (title, ISBN lookup, condition, price, photos, pickup/delivery options).
- Real‑time ISBN lookup via Google Books API to auto‑populate book details.
- Draft autosave and preview before publishing.

## ✅ Search, Filter & Course Mapping
- Full‑text search powered by Elasticsearch for title, author, ISBN, and description.
- Filters for price range, condition, location, and delivery method.
- Course mapping UI that lets students tag listings to a specific course (e.g., "CS101 – Intro to Programming").

## ✅ In‑App Messaging & Escrow Payment
- Secure messaging thread tied to each listing, with read receipts.
- Integrated Stripe Connect escrow: buyer funds are held until the seller marks the item shipped and the buyer confirms receipt.
- Automated release of funds and email notifications.

## ✅ Rating, Review & Admin Moderation Dashboard
- Post‑transaction rating system (1‑5 stars) and optional text review.
- Admin panel to view flagged listings, manage user bans, and edit marketplace policies.
- Dashboard analytics: total listings, transactions, and average rating per user.

# Why this was needed
- **Student verification** prevents fraud and ensures a trusted community.
- A **guided listing wizard** reduces friction, encouraging more listings and accurate data.
- **Search and course mapping** make it fast for buyers to find the exact edition they need, cutting down on time spent scrolling.
- **Escrow payments** protect both parties, addressing the biggest pain point in peer‑to‑peer textbook sales.
- **Ratings and moderation** maintain quality, encourage good behavior, and give the admin team tools to keep the marketplace safe.

# Testing & Documentation
- Added unit tests for verification flow, listing creation, and escrow state transitions (90% coverage).
- End‑to‑end Cypress tests cover the full buyer‑seller transaction lifecycle.
- Updated the `README.md` with setup instructions, environment variables, and API endpoint documentation.

# Next steps
- Mobile app wrapper for iOS/Android.
- Integration with university campus card for optional payment method.
- Loyalty program for repeat sellers.

body:
## Summary
- Add JavaScript cross-file taint analysis following the same two-pass scanner pattern established for Python in PR #87
- Pass 1 extracts `FunctionTaintSummary` for exported functions in JS files by running synthetic taint analysis per parameter against all JS taint rule sinks
- Pass 2 resolves `require('./services')` and `import { fn } from './services'` to file paths, then checks cross-file summaries when an imported function is called with tainted arguments
- Refactors all 8 JS taint rules to use a shared `map_js_taint_findings` helper with cross-file support (mirroring Python's `map_taint_findings`)

## Key changes
- `src/rules/javascript_taint.rs`: `CrossFileInfo`, `analyze_tree_with_cross_file()`, `extract_cross_file_summaries()`, `resolve_js_imports_to_paths()`, cross-file call handling, exported function collection (CJS `module.exports` + ESM `export`)
- `src/rules/javascript.rs`: `map_js_taint_findings()` shared helper, `js_taint_rule_specs()` for pass 1

body:
## Summary
- Problem: Feishu had two regressions in the same flow: repeated tool/hook registration on plugin cache misses, and named-account config loads silently rewrote top-level `groupPolicy: "open"` back to `allowlist`.
- Why it matters: repeated registrations add log noise and risk duplicate side effects, while the `groupPolicy` rewrite blocks group replies even when the user explicitly configured Feishu groups to stay open.
- What changed: added an idempotency guard around Feishu `registerFull`, declared Feishu-specific named-account promotion keys, added the early promotion fallback used by legacy config loading, and locked the behavior with regression tests.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not change generic promotion behavior for other channels, and it does not alter Feishu routing or security defaults outside the named-account migration path.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #56520
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Feishu `registerFull` had no idempotency guard when plugin loader cache misses caused re-registration, and Feishu had no named-account promotion contract, so legacy config normalization treated shared top-level policy keys like single-account fields and moved `groupPolicy` into `accounts.default`.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no regression coverage for repeated Feishu full registration or for loading a named-account Feishu config with top-level `groupPolicy: "open"`.
- Contributing context (if known): the live config on the affected machine used `channels.feishu.defaultAccount = "main"` with named `main`/`candy` accounts and a top-level `groupPolicy`, which hits the legacy promotion path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `extensions/feishu/index.test.ts`, `extensions/feishu/src/setup-surface.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.migrations.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: rerunning Feishu full registration must not duplicate tools/hooks, and loading Feishu named-account configs must preserve top-level `groupPolicy` and avoid synthesizing `accounts.default`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug lives in the entry registration seam and the legacy config normalization seam; both are reproducible without booting the full gateway.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Feishu group messages respect a top-level `channels.feishu.groupPolicy` again when named accounts are configured.
- Feishu tools and subagent hooks no longer re-register repeatedly when plugin cache misses cause `registerFull` to rerun.

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu Linux
- Runtime/container: Node v24.14.0, local gateway service
- Model/provider: minimax/MiniMax-M2.7
- Integration/channel (if any): Feishu (websocket mode)
- Relevant config (redacted): `channels.feishu.defaultAccount = "main"`, named `main`/`candy` accounts, top-level `groupPolicy = "open"`, wildcard group route with `requireMention = false`

### Steps

1. Configure Feishu with named accounts and a top-level `groupPolicy: "open"`.
2. Start the gateway and load config through the normal runtime path.
3. Send a Feishu group message and watch the runtime config and gateway logs.

### Expected

- Top-level `channels.feishu.groupPolicy` stays `open`.
- No synthetic `channels.feishu.accounts.default` is created.
- Feishu group messages are accepted under the configured open policy.
- Feishu tools/hooks register once per process.

### Actual

- Before the fix, runtime config rewrote the top-level `groupPolicy` to `allowlist`, created `accounts.default.groupPolicy = "open"`, and dropped group messages with `groupPolicy=allowlist` logs.
- Before the fix, repeated Feishu tool registration logs appeared when full registration reran.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: reproduced the bad loaded runtime config on the affected machine, patched the code, confirmed both `src` and `dist` `loadConfig()` preserved top-level `groupPolicy: "open"`, restarted the live gateway service, and confirmed Feishu messages started arriving again.
- Edge cases checked: named-account Feishu config without an existing `default` account, shared top-level auth plus shared top-level policy, repeated `registerFull` calls.
- What you did **not** verify: webhook mode and account-specific `groupPolicy` overrides were not retested in a live environment.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Feishu named-account promotion now keeps shared top-level auth/policy fields in place instead of synthesizing `accounts.default`.
  - Mitigation: the change is limited to Feishu, the early fallback matches the Feishu setup contract, and regression tests cover both the migration seam and the entry registration seam.

author: jkordish
body:
This PR addresses the concrete findings from the exhaustive Rust review and closes the missing verification gaps without pulling unrelated dirty worktree changes into the branch.

The main user-facing issue was that two supposedly observational flows were not behaving observationally. Building live UI state would eagerly interrupt stale AI runs, and both the no-TTY TUI fallback and the live-store snapshot path flowed through that mutating startup logic. In practice that meant rendering state for inspection could rewrite persisted AI run state. This change separates read-only live-state construction from the explicit recovery path, keeps interruption behavior for the interactive startup that actually owns that responsibility, and adds regression coverage proving the read-only paths preserve active runs.

The second production bug was in the Oura OAuth loopback callback flow. When callback waiting timed out or the channel closed early, the code returned before sending shutdown to the spawned callback server and before awaiting the server task. That could leave the callback listener alive and keep the port occupied, causing retries to fail for reasons that were hard to diagnose. The callback wait logic now always tears the server down before returning, and the new timeout regression test proves the port is released and immediately reusable.

This PR also removes a cross-cutting source of date-window drift. Local-day resolution was duplicated across several modules with a silent fallback to UTC whenever local offset discovery failed. That made "today"-scoped behavior harder to reason about and could shift review and snapshot windows around midnight on hosts with incomplete local time configuration. The behavior is now centralized in a single helper with deterministic tests and a single documented fallback path.

To make release hygiene explicit rather than ambient, this branch adds repo-owned `audit.toml` and `deny.toml` policy files. `cargo audit` is now configured to acknowledge the still-upstream `RUSTSEC-2026-0097` `rand 0.8.5` advisory path while keeping the exception visible and documented. `cargo deny check` is configured for the current dependency and licensing policy so the repo can enforce that intentionally.

Validation performed for this branch:

- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --all`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features`
- `cargo run -- doctor`
- `cargo audit`
- `cargo deny check`
- `cargo package --allow-dirty --list`
- `cargo package --allow-dirty`

The only remaining explicit risk is the documented upstream audit exception for `oauth2`/`rand 0.8.5`; everything else identified in the review is fixed and covered here.

#define BLOCK_SIZE 32

constexpr int kBlockSize = 32;

body:
### Motivation
- Make combined predictions handling robust across multiple dated snapshots and avoid accidental data loss when rebuilding cumulative combined files.  
- Improve local strategy parameter selection using walk-forward stability checks and align shortlist filtering with historical evaluation.  
- Harden outputs by enforcing CSV schema validation and more consistent file writing and logging.

### Description
- Reworked combined CSV loading to read all dated `combined_nba_predictions_acc_*.csv` snapshots up to the target date, concatenate them and deduplicate by `date, home_team, away_team`; added `_read_combined_snapshot` and `_normalize_combined_schema` helpers to standardize columns and capture `source_snapshot_date`.  
- Introduced walk-forward/local-search utilities: `_iter_param_grid`, `_evaluate_params_on_subset`, `find_best_local_params_walk_forward` and `evaluate_strategy_stability` to select and validate local parameter sets using multi-split testing and stability gates; integrated these into the local parameter selection flow while preserving a global fallback.  
- Aligned shortlist filtering with historical logic by forcing the effective probability threshold to respect the clipping floor (`PROB_CLIP_LO`).  
- Added CSV output hardening: always write with `lineterminator="\n"` and validate produced files with `validate_structured_csv` to ensure required columns and minimal data rows.  
- Improved date handling and snapshot semantics by clearly separating requested run date vs resolved source snapshot date and using the source snapshot when rebuilding combined data.

### Motivation
- Provide a headless-friendly monitor that connects to an existing Chromium/Chrome/Edge session via CDP and captures call-history rows from a web UI.
- Persist new calls and interpreter status changes into an Excel file with computed amounts and multiple reporting sheets for daily, weekly and monthly summaries.
- Offer robust parsing and deduplication so visible rows can be synchronized into a single source of truth without duplicating entries.
- Ship usage instructions for launching the browser with remote debugging and examples to run the monitor.

### Description
- Adds `monitor_call_log.py`, a comprehensive script that connects via Playwright CDP (`connect_over_cdp`), finds the target page, parses `mat-table` rows, normalizes call records into `CallRecord`, computes `Amount USD` using `RATE_PER_MINUTE`, and deduplicates by a `Unique Key`.
- Implements live status capture by listening to network requests, parsing status payloads into `StatusEvent`, recording `Status Log` and computing `Status Durations` including logic to persist only real changes and avoid duplicates.
- Creates and maintains an Excel workbook (`openpyxl`) with sheets `Calls`, `Daily Summary`, `Status Log`, `Status Durations`, `Monthly Call Summary`, `Weekly Available Summary`, and `Weekly Available Detail`, plus formatting, KPI cards and basic charts; provides functions to rebuild summaries (`rebuild_daily_summary`, `rebuild_monthly_call_summary`, `rebuild_weekly_available_summary`).
- Adds `README.md` with dependency installation, instructions to start Chrome/Edge with `--remote-debugging-port`, example command line usage `py monitor_call_log.py --cdp-url http://127.0.0.1:9222 --url-contains "/call-history" --excel call_log.xlsx --interval 180`, and description of output columns and sheets.

author: zgriffiin
body:
## What changed

Implemented hybrid truth model for session progress so UI can track live runtime state without waiting on durable orchestration replay.

- added thread-progress contracts and websocket RPCs for snapshot + subscription
- added a server-side `ThreadProgressTracker` that normalizes provider runtime into per-thread live progress snapshots
- separated `agent_running`, waiting, recovery, and post-run phases
- tracked explicit post-run stages for assistant finalize, checkpoint capture, and quality gate work
- bootstrapped and subscribed to thread progress separately from orchestration history on web client
- hardened websocket unary request timeouts and reconnect behavior for replay/snapshot recovery
- updated chat UI to use effective live progress for labels, timers, working row, and stop-button behavior
- updated touched tests and harnesses for new tracker wiring

## Why changed

UI drift still happened because durable orchestration state was being used as both history and liveness source. That made replay stalls, delayed projections, and post-run work look like the agent was still actively generating output.

This change makes durable orchestration state remain source of truth for history, while live thread-progress snapshots become source of truth for current phase and recovery state.

## User impact

- UI should converge to CLI truth much faster
- waiting for approval/input no longer renders as generic active work
- post-run checks now show explicit state instead of looking like model output is still running
- reconnect/recovery paths should recover automatically instead of requiring tab reload in common timeout cases
- stop button now only appears when there is meaningful work to stop

## Root cause

Root issue was mixed responsibilities:

- orchestration projection used for both reloadable history and real-time liveness
- replay/snapshot recovery could stall transport requests without hard timeout enforcement
- coarse `running` session state was too broad and masked waiting/recovery/post-run phases

## Validation

- `bun fmt`
- `bun lint`
- `bun typecheck`
- `bun run test -- src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.logic.test.ts src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.test.tsx` in `apps/web`
- `bun run test -- src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationReactor.test.ts src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.test.ts src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.test.ts` in `apps/server`

## Remaining follow-up

- add dedicated `ThreadProgressTracker` unit coverage
- add full recovery timeout and polling cadence regression tests
- continue through remaining acceptance and recovery scenarios

author: irongollem
body:
Stacked on top of #134. Extracts the list-page skeleton that every list view in the app currently duplicates.

> I'll re-target this to `main` once #134 is merged — until then it's based on that branch so it can build on the new primitives (`useBreakpoint`, safe-area utilities, `ListActionButton`-friendly responsive bar).

## Background

The audit in #132 identified that 14 list views (NPCs, Monsters, Items, Notes, Scriptorium, Locations, Quests, Spells, Traps, Puzzles, Factions, Rules, Hall of Heroes, Species) all follow the same skeleton:

```
Title + description + actions  ← sticky
───── gold divider ─────
[search] [filter] [filter] [Clear]  ← sticky (if present)
─────────────────────────
list body
```

`PageHeader.vue` was a first pass at this abstraction, but it only owns the title/divider/sticky-slot framing. Everything else — button styling, filter row markup, mobile overflow behaviour — was copy-pasted across 14 views, each independently breaking on mobile.

## What this adds

### `src/components/common/ListPageLayout.vue`

The complete list-page shell.

- **Sticky header** with mobile-first padding (`pt-3 md:pt-6`) and smaller title on mobile (`text-xl md:text-3xl`) — addresses the audit finding that headers ate ~50% of viewport on phones.
- **Action row overflow** — capped at `max-w-[70%]` on mobile with `overflow-x-auto`; action bars no longer push buttons off the viewport. Negative-margin trick extends the scroll area to the edge so content isn't clipped by the outer `px-4`.
- **DiceRoller auto-mount** — every list page had it; now it's a prop (`showDiceRoller`, default `true`).
- Slots: `actions`, `filters` (free-form, caller controls layout), default (body), `footer` (optional).

### `src/components/common/ListActionButton.vue`

Collapses the three duplicated button styles into one component:

| `variant` | Use | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | The one CTA per page ("New NPC") | Label always visible |
| `secondary` (default) | Outlined — Generate / Import / Populate | Icon-only on `<sm` |
| `ghost` | Subtle — "Clear filters" | Icon-only on `<sm` (override with `collapseOnMobile={false}`) |

Renders as `<RouterLink>` when `to` is set, `<a>` when `href` is set, `<button>` otherwise.

Directly addresses your "icon buttons on mobile" request — non-primary actions collapse their labels below `sm`, keeping the tappable icon + `title`/`aria-label` intact for accessibility.

## Migrations

- **NotesView** — simplest case (one primary action, no filters). 22 → 16 lines.
- **MonstersView** — representative case (primary + secondary action, search + 2 filter groups, Clear). 98 → 92 lines.

Filter markup stays mostly unchanged in Monsters — extracting `ListSearchInput` / `ListFilterGroup` / `ListFilterRow` is queued for the next PR so this one stays reviewable. The remaining 12 list views keep `PageHeader` for now; migration is incremental.

## Intentionally not in this PR

- `ListSearchInput`, `ListFilterGroup`, `ListFilterRow` primitives — next PR
- Views with outliers (Rules tabs, Quests view-toggle, HallOfHeroes footer, Traps/Puzzles/Factions inline grids) — each gets its own small follow-up once primitives are in place
- `PageHeader` deprecation — keep it working; migration is opt-in per view

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — passes
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- [ ] Manual: Notes page at 375px / 768px / 1280px — header compact, single action visible
- [ ] Manual: Monsters page at 375px — Generate becomes icon-only, New Monster stays labelled, filter row scrolls horizontally when it overflows
- [ ] Manual: Desktop regression — both views look identical to before at ≥md
- [ ] Verify sticky header still sticks when scrolling the list

author: livepeer-tessa
body:
## Problem

Closes #922.

When a LoRA trained for Wan2.1-**5B** (`in_features=5120`) is loaded into the Wan2.1-**1.3B** model (`in_features=1536`), `peft_lora.py` successfully loads the adapter (layer names match) but then fails at inference with:

```
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (768x1536 and 5120x32)
```

This produced **156 identical errors** in session `067a55be` (14:41–14:55 UTC today) while consuming GPU resources the entire time — with no user-visible error message.

## Root Cause

`parse_lora_weights()` matched LoRA layer names to model parameters without checking that the weight shapes were compatible. The mismatch (`lora_A.shape[1] != model_weight.shape[1]`) only surfaced later during the `torch.mm` call inside `peft/tuners/lora/layer.py`.

## Fix

Add dimension validation inside `parse_lora_weights()` immediately after a match is found. If the LoRA's `in_features` or `out_features` don't match the model layer's weight shape, raise a `ValueError` with a user-readable message naming the layer, the LoRA dimensions, the model dimensions, and a plain-language hint about model architecture mismatch.

**Before:**
```
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (768x1536 and 5120x32)
  File peft/tuners/lora/layer.py, line 807, in forward
  ... (at inference, 156 times)
```

**After:**
```
ValueError: LoRA dimension mismatch at layer 'blocks.0.self_attn.q':
LoRA expects (256x5120) but model layer is (256x1536).
This LoRA was likely trained for a different model size (e.g. Wan2.1-5B vs 1.3B).
Please use a LoRA that matches the loaded model architecture.
  (raised at load time, before inference starts)
```

The `ValueError` propagates through `PeftLoRAStrategy.load_adapters_from_list` (caught → `RuntimeError: LoRA loading failed`) and through `PermanentMergeLoRAStrategy` the same way.

## Tests

5 new unit tests in `tests/test_lora_dimension_validation.py`:
- Compatible LoRA loads without error
- 5B LoRA on 1.3B model raises `ValueError`
- Error message names the layer and both dimension sets
- Out-features mismatch is also caught
- 5B LoRA on 5B model is fine

All 5 pass locally.

## About the PR
<!-- What did you change? -->
Now silo produce: 1.5 steel, glass and plastic per minute (90 per hour), 0.2 cloth, gold, silver, plasma and uranium per minute (12 per hour), 0.02 diamonds per minute (1.2 per hour).

## Why / Balance
<!-- Discuss how this would affect game balance or explain why it was changed. Link any relevant discussions or issues. -->
This change is intended for cases where cargo is a total skill issue. It should not replace miners or technicians (2 hours of waiting will bring less than a crate of gold). But it should allow you to get minimal resources for some buildings or instruments. I know that you can disassemble lockers for steel, melt light bulbs into glass, boil plastic in chemmaster, and get plasma, silver, and bluespace crystals from slimes. But it doesn't seem to me that this is what departments should be doing every 4th round (at least on the server I'm playing on).
90 plastic, steel and glass per hour is 1 crate, I think this should be enough, it can also be reduced to 60 per hour.
0.2 precious materials per minute is 1 in 5 minutes, this should be enough for single boards like a chemmaster, industrial ore processor and experimental anomaly vessel, perhaps even enough for hyperconvection and small amounts of advanced chemicals.
I'm not sure about cloth, it's used quite rarely, but sometimes it comes in handy for duracloth, fultons and suits, if HOP is kind. I think 12 per hour will be enough, although more is possible.
As for diamonds, I'm not sure if they should be there at all, but they are enough for 1 gygax per hour or 12 bluespace crystals with hyperconvection.

body:
## Summary

Fixed 7 documentation consistency issues discovered during analysis of color comparison options.

## Changes

- **Fix incorrect default tolerance** — docs said 0.0005, code uses 0.001
- **Add decision tree** for choosing between perceptual_threshold vs color_distance_limit
- **Clarify tolerance relationship** — works with both color methods (not exclusive as docs claimed); applied by default for VIPS
- **Correct color_distance_limit scale** — 0-441 → 0-510 (RGBA, not RGB)
- **Document driver difference** — VIPS counts actual different pixels, ChunkyPNG counts diff bounding box area
- **Fix misleading example** — drivers.md used tolerance 0.3, 600× more permissive than recommendations
- **Add missing YARD docs** — perceptual_threshold option undocumented in DSL
- **Fix copy-paste errors** — test named 'color threshold' demonstrating shift_distance_limit

## Files Changed

- README.md
- docs/configuration.md
- docs/drivers.md
- lib/capybara_screenshot_diff/dsl.rb

## Summary by Sourcery

Clarify and correct documentation around visual diff color comparison options and their interactions.

Documentation:
- Update configuration and README docs to show accurate defaults and recommended values for tolerance and perceptual_threshold.
- Document the decision process for choosing between perceptual_threshold and color_distance_limit, including their exclusivity and differing scales.
- Explain how tolerance behaves across VIPS and ChunkyPNG drivers, including the stricter bounding-box behavior in ChunkyPNG.
- Correct scales and semantics for color_distance_limit (RGBA 0-510) and add clearer usage examples with realistic tolerance values.
- Add missing DSL option documentation for perceptual_threshold, color_distance_limit, and tolerance in the screenshot helper YARD docs.

author: jpollock
body:
Closes #5

## What

Adds `nexus doctor` — a single command that shows system health at a glance and tells new users what to do next.

```
Nexus AI v0.2.1 — System Health
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ✅  Local app           Installed
  ✅  Local running       Running
  ✅  Nexus AI addon      Active (v0.2.1)
  ✅  GraphQL server      Connected (port 4000)
  ✅  MCP server          Running · 161 tools
  ✅  AI agent config     Claude Desktop
  ✅  AI provider         Anthropic (Claude)
  ✅  Local Gateway       Enabled
  ✅  Sites with AI       4 / 32 sites configured · 0 running
──────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Everything looks good. 🎉
```

Every `⚠️` or `❌` line includes the exact command to fix it. First-run state (nothing configured) shows a numbered getting-started guide.

## Checks

- **Local installed/running** — `isLocalInstalled()` / `isLocalRunning()`
- **Addon active** — `isAddonActivated()` (handles both npm-global and Local addons-dir installs); version via `getInstalledAddonVersion()` with npm-global fallback
- **GraphQL** — `readConnectionInfo()` + connectivity
- **MCP server** — reads `nexus-ai-mcp-connection-info.json`, pings `/health`
- **AI agent config** — file-based agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf) + `claude mcp list` for Claude Code
- **AI provider** — `nexusAiGetConfig` mutation; checks key present
- **Gateway** — same mutation
- **Sites with AI** — `nexusSitesList` + reads `nexus-ai_site_ai_config.json` from disk; shows `N / total configured · X running`

## Behaviour

- Each check is isolated — one failure never blocks others
- Skips bootstrap (handles its own connection logic, works when Local is not running)
- `--json` flag for machine-readable output
- Exits with code 1 if any check is `error` status

## Docs updated

- `README.md` — `nexus doctor` replaces `nexus sites list` as post-install verification; `nexus mcp setup` surfaced as next step
- `docs/user-guide/getting-started.md` — two-journey orientation (MCP in 2 min vs WordPress AI in 5 min); npm install as primary path; verification section
- `docs/user-guide/troubleshooting.md` — "Start Here: run nexus doctor" at the top
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry under [0.2.1] Added

## Test plan

- [ ] `nexus doctor` on healthy system shows all ✅
- [ ] `nexus doctor` when Local not running shows graceful degradation (checks 1-5 still complete)
- [ ] `nexus doctor` with no AI provider shows ⚠️ with `nexus ai config` next step
- [ ] `nexus doctor --json` produces valid JSON with all check results
- [ ] `nexus doctor` with no agents configured shows ⚠️ with `nexus mcp setup` next step
- [ ] First-run state (MCP not configured + no AI provider) shows getting-started guide

author: lawrence3699
body:
Fixes #1225

**Failing scenario:** A single-line comment (`// test`) at the end of a Dart file without a trailing newline is not tokenized as `CommentSingle`.

**Root cause:** The pattern `//.*?\n` requires a literal `\n`. With `dot_all: true`, the negated character class `[^\n]` is used instead of `.` to avoid matching across lines.

**Before:** `// test` at EOF → not matched, falls through to other rules
**After:** `// test` at EOF → correctly matched as `CommentSingle`

**Why the fix is correct:** `//[^\n]*\n?` matches from `//` to end-of-line using a negated character class (unaffected by `dot_all`), and the optional `\n?` preserves the existing behavior of including the trailing newline in the token when present.

**Validation:**
- `go test ./lexers/ -run TestLexers/Dart` — PASS
- `go test ./lexers/ -run TestLexers` (full suite) — PASS
- Manual verification: both `// test\n` and `// test<EOF>` tokenize correctly

author: afc-afc0
body:
* Fixes TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGameCode#2346

  DumbProjectileBehavior does not serialize `m_flightPath` (the Bezier curve points) or `m_currentFlightPathStep` (the current      
  position along the path). On load, `m_flightPath` is empty and `m_currentFlightPathStep` is 0, so the first `update()` call       
  evaluates `0 >= 0` as true and immediately calls `detonate()`. This is most visible with slow artillery like Inferno Cannons and  
  Nuke Cannons.

  The fix adds two things:

  1. Serializes `m_currentFlightPathStep` in `xfer()` (version bumped from 1 to 2) so the projectile knows where it was along its   
  flight path.
  2. Rebuilds the flight path Bezier curve in `loadPostProcess()` using the already-saved start, end, segments and speed parameters.

  Old saves (version 1) remain compatible — the step defaults to 0 and the path is rebuilt, so projectiles restart from the
  beginning of their arc rather than detonating instantly.

  ## Test
  - Built and launched Zero Hour
  - Started a skirmish and built artillery units
  - Fired artillery and immediately saved the game while shells were mid-flight
  - Loaded the save — projectiles continued their flight path and landed at their target without instant detonation
  - Verified loading old saves works correctly — projectiles restart from the beginning of their arc instead of detonating

author: mittalrishabh
body:
## Task 2.1 — Tiered Read Path

NVMe-first, S3-fallback read path with optional hydration.

### TieredReadHandler
- **NVMe fast path**: Read directly if chunk is on NVMe
- **S3 fallback**: Fetch via S3PhysicalDev::read() → ChunkStore::get() if chunk not on NVMe
- **Hydration**: Optionally write S3 data back to NVMe for fast subsequent reads
- **NVMe failure fallthrough**: If NVMe read fails, falls back to S3 (handles corruption)

### Configuration
- `s3_read_fallback_enabled` (bool) — enable/disable S3 fallback
- `s3_hydrate_on_read` (bool) — enable/disable write-back to NVMe
- Runtime-changeable via `set_config()`

### API
- `async_read()` — returns `Future<pair<error_code, byte_array>>`
- `sync_read()` — blocking read into pre-allocated buffer
- `hydrate()` — force-download from S3 and write to NVMe (pre-warming)

### NvmeDeviceIO Interface
Abstract interface isolating TieredReadHandler from PhysicalDev. Enables clean testing.

### Metrics
- `s3_read_fallback_count`, `s3_hydrate_count`, `nvme_read_count`
- `s3_read_fallback_latency_us`, `nvme_read_latency_us` histograms
- `tiered_read_errors`, `s3_hydrate_failures`

### Tests (12)
NVMe fast path, S3 fallback, hydration on/off, force hydrate, NVMe failure fallthrough, sync/async paths, runtime config change

author: alegd
body:
## Summary

Addresses the low-severity items surfaced by the OWASP/architecture audit. Six small improvements, no user-facing behavior changes — all hardening against malformed input, leaky errors, and missing session context.

## Items included

1. **Multer file-size limit** — reject oversized uploads at the FileInterceptor before buffering into memory. Extracted \`MAX_FILE_SIZE\` and \`ALLOWED_MIMETYPES\` to \`audio.constants.ts\` to share between interceptor and service.
2. **Resend error handling** — \`EmailService.sendOtp\` now inspects the Resend response and throws on error. Silent email failures were possible before.
3. **Jira Zod validation** — every Jira response (tokens, accessible resources, projects, created issues) is validated with Zod schemas in \`jira.schemas.ts\`. Malformed responses fail fast.
4. **Jira error wrapping** — callers now see a user-friendly \`BadRequestException\`; the full upstream payload is logged. Prevents accidental leaks of internal Jira error details.
5. **RefreshToken session context** — \`userAgent\` and \`ipAddress\` are now populated from the request on \`verifyOtp\`, \`completeRegister\`, and \`refresh\`. Fields existed in the schema but were always null.
6. **Frontend timezone** — replaces hardcoded \`Europe/Vienna\` with \`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone\` (falls back to UTC).

## Deferred (out of scope)

Scalability items in the same ticket — Redis-backed \`CacheService\`, S3 \`StorageAdapter\`, frontend JWT refresh mutex — were deferred because they only matter under horizontal scaling, which is out of scope for the MVP.

## Jira

YAP-106 — Tech debt: low-priority security and scalability improvements

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass: API 201 → **203**, Web **346**
- [x] Type-check clean across monorepo
- [ ] Upload a >50MB file → rejected by Multer with 413 (instead of the old "read into memory then check size" path)
- [ ] Verify Sessions endpoint surfaces \`userAgent\`/\`ipAddress\` for new tokens
- [ ] Trigger Jira with a deliberately bad token → response is a generic \`BadRequestException\`; raw details only in server log

## Tests added

5 new tests:
- \`EmailService\`: response error, rejection
- \`JiraService\`: malformed token response, leaky 401 body
- \`AuthService\`: refresh token stores userAgent + ipAddress when context is provided

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a modern, publishable Python package layout for the MTO-CL optimizer using the `src` layout and PEP 517/621 packaging metadata. 
- Break the original monolithic script into focused modules to improve importability, reuse, and maintenance while keeping the algorithmic core unchanged. 
- Declare runtime dependencies (`numpy`, `pandas`) and standard project metadata so the package can be built and distributed.

### Description
- Add `pyproject.toml` configured with `setuptools.build_meta`, project metadata (name `mtocl-optimizer`, version `0.0.1`, MIT license, `requires-python >=3.9`) and dependencies `numpy` and `pandas`.
- Create `src/mtocl_optimizer/` package and public exports in `__init__.py` for `MTOCLConfig`, `BaseObjectiveFunction`, `FunctionWrapper`, `DataFittingObjective`, and `MTOCLOptimizer`.
- Split the implementation into modules: `config.py` (defines `MTOCLConfig`), `objectives.py` (contains `BaseObjectiveFunction`, `FunctionWrapper`, `DataFittingObjective` with NumPy-based logic and bounds handling), and `optimizer.py` (contains `MTOCLOptimizer`, typed `OptimizationResult`, vectorized Fixed-Offspring topology, Climate Change elimination/distortion, and pandas CSV export), using package-relative imports.
- Update `README.md` with placeholder badges, algorithm overview (Fixed-Offspring topology and Climate Change phases), installation & usage example (showing `MTOCLConfig`, `MTOCLOptimizer`, `FunctionWrapper`), and the Korani (2021) thesis reference, and ensure an MIT `LICENSE` is present.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall src` which succeeded and compiled all new modules without syntax errors. 
- Performed a runtime smoke test invocation (`PYTHONPATH=src python - <<'PY' ... PY`) which could not complete because `numpy` is not installed in the execution environment. 
- No additional automated unit tests were added or executed in this change.

author: yazzaoui
body:
## Human Summary
Remove the live receipt retry-owner / delivery-backfill compatibility bridge from the pending-delivery and receipt hot path. Pending-delivery reads now use the canonical delivery/receipt owner directly, and receipt writes fail closed instead of manufacturing or repairing delivery ownership from receipt state.

Closes #360
Part of #157

## What Changed
- removed `normalizeLegacyAgentRetryOwners(...)` from:
  - `ListPendingEventsForAgent(...)`
  - `ListPendingSubscribedEvents(...)`
  - `ListPendingAgentDeliveryFacts(...)`
- removed the live bridge helpers from `internal/store/event_receipt_store.go`:
  - `ensureAgentDeliveryRetryOwnerTx(...)`
  - `backfillLegacyAgentDeliveryFromReceiptTx(...)`
  - the now-dead receipt-state lock helper used only by that bridge
- changed `upsertAgentReceiptSpec(...)` to fail closed when the canonical agent delivery row is missing instead of manufacturing or backfilling delivery ownership from receipt state
- rewrote legacy bridge regressions to canonical-owner regressions and added a delivery-facts proof for legacy receipt-only state

## Why This Is Needed
The current seam was still letting receipt state front the canonical delivery/receipt owner in both pending-delivery reads and receipt writes. That preserved a live compatibility boundary in a store hot path and kept ownership ambiguous. This PR removes that bridge and leaves one canonical owner path in the touched seam.

## Scope Boundaries
In scope:
- receipt retry-owner / delivery-backfill compatibility removal in pending-delivery reads and receipt writes
- canonical fail-closed behavior when delivery ownership is missing

Out of scope:
- explicit schema-capability boundary cleanup
- task-conversation visibility mixed-rollout cleanup
- broad event store redesign

## Spec References
- `docs/specs/swarm-platform/platform/contracts/platform-spec.yaml: engine.event_loop.lifecycle.step_6.agent_delivery`
- `docs/specs/swarm-platform/platform/contracts/platform-spec.yaml: engine.event_loop.crash_recovery`
- `docs/specs/swarm-platform/platform/contracts/platform-spec.yaml: engine.error_model.handler_execution_failure.retry_policy`
- `docs/specs/swarm-platform/platform/contracts/platform-spec.yaml: platform_tables.tables.event_deliveries`
- `docs/specs/swarm-platform/platform/contracts/platform-spec.yaml: platform_tables.tables.event_receipts`
- `docs/specs/swarm-platform/platform/contracts/platform-spec.yaml: run_model.lifecycle.completion`

## Tests Run
- `go test ./internal/store -run 'Test(UpsertEventReceipt_AlignsRetryOwnershipOnCanonicalDelivery_V2|UpsertEventReceipt_FailsClosedOnLegacyReceiptOnlyRetryHistory_V2|PendingAgentEvents_IgnoreLegacyReceiptOnlyRetryOwner_V2|ListPendingAgentDeliveryFacts_IgnoresLegacyReceiptOnlyRetryOwner_V2|ListPendingAgentDeliveryFacts_AlignsWithCanonicalPendingStates_V2|ListPendingEventsForAgent_InProgressWithoutReceipt_RemainsPending|EventReceipts_RetryToDeadLetter_AndPendingQueries)$' -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/store ./internal/runtime ./internal/dashboard/server -count=1`
- `go test ./... -count=1`

## Residual Risk
- Parent `#157` remains open for at least two sibling classes:
  - task-conversation visibility mixed-rollout cleanup
  - broader schema-capability boundary cleanup / decomposition follow-up
- This PR does not claim closure for those sibling classes.

## Follow-Up
- Continue parent `#157` with the remaining sibling compatibility classes after this child merges.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve robustness of plan input handling by surfacing structured errors for common malformed fields and ambiguous fight dates.
- Ensure date-only fight dates are interpreted deterministically by requiring an explicit athlete timezone or rejecting ambiguous payloads.
- Preserve provenance for inferred values so downstream systems can reason about which inputs were user-supplied vs system-inferred.

### Description
- Added `PlanInputValidationError` for structured validation failures and used it to signal specific error codes for clients. 
- Introduced `_normalize_payload`, `_validate_training_frequency`, and `_validate_fight_timing_strategy` helpers to centralize normalization and validation logic for plan inputs. 
- Enforced: training frequency must parse as an integer when provided, otherwise it is inferred from `Training Availability` and the inference is recorded in `parsing_metadata`. 
- For date-only fight dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) require a non-empty `Athlete Time Zone` that resolves to an IANA zone or UTC offset; otherwise reject with a specific error code. 
- Added `parsing_metadata` to `PlanInput` to record sources for fields like `training_frequency` and `athlete_timezone`. 
- Updated `generate_plan_sync` to catch `PlanInputValidationError` and return a controlled invalid result with `missing_fields` containing the structured error code. 
- Minor imports and dataclass adjustments (`field`) and a README note advising inclusion of `Athlete Time Zone` for date-only fight dates. 
- Test data and unit tests were updated to cover the new validation behavior and metadata expectations.

### Testing
- Ran the test suite with `pytest`, including the updated `tests/test_input_parsing.py` and `tests/test_conditioning_diagnostics.py` which add coverage for invalid training frequency format and timezone strategy errors, and all tests passed. 
- New assertions verify that invalid numeric frequency yields an `invalid_training_frequency_format` error code, that missing timezone for date-only fight dates yields `missing_timezone_strategy`, and that invalid timezone strings yield `invalid_timezone_strategy`. 
- Confirmed existing behavior around inference of `training_frequency` from `Training Availability` and that `parsing_metadata` records the inference source.

author: chrisgeo
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `src/lib/api.ts` had a static top-level `import { auth } from "@/lib/auth"` which caused Turbopack to include `auth.ts` in client-side bundles. Since `process.env.AUTH_SECRET` is never available in the browser (only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are), the module-level IIFE threw on every dashboard page load.
- **Fix (api.ts)**: Replace the static import with a dynamic `getAuth()` helper using `await import("@/lib/auth")` so the bundler no longer traces `auth.ts` into client chunks.
- **Defense-in-depth (auth.ts)**: Replace the eager-throwing IIFE with an `undefined` fallback in production — lets Auth.js validate the secret lazily per-request instead of killing the entire module at import time.

## Leak chain

```
dashboard/page.tsx → CockpitClient ("use client") → EvidencePanel ("use client")
  → import { getExplainData } from "@/lib/api"
    → import { auth } from "@/lib/auth"  ← static, evaluates immediately in browser
      → authSecret IIFE throws (no process.env.AUTH_SECRET client-side)
```

## Verification

- Confirmed `AUTH_SECRET` is set in the container (`env | grep AUTH_SECRET`)
- Error stack trace shows Turbopack client-side module evaluation (`01qefuf7yjwj4.js`, `turbopack-*`)
- All other static imports of `@/lib/auth` are in `"use server"` modules or server-component-only pages — no other leak paths

SCREENSHOT-WAIVER: Bug fix — no UI changes, only fixes runtime error in browser console
TEST-WAIVER: Import boundary fix — no testable logic change; existing auth and API tests still pass

author: copilot
body:
The site was deploying successfully in CI but remained inaccessible publicly because deployment strategy and repository Pages source were out of sync. This change switches publishing to the native GitHub Pages artifact/deploy flow so the live site is served from the expected source.

- **Deployment source alignment**
  - Replaced branch-push publishing (`peaceiris/actions-gh-pages`) with the official Pages pipeline (`configure-pages` → `upload-pages-artifact` → `deploy-pages`).
  - Split workflow into `build` and `deploy` jobs with `needs: build` to match GitHub Pages deployment semantics.

- **Pages runtime permissions**
  - Updated workflow permissions to include `pages: write` and `id-token: write` (and reduced `contents` to `read`) for OIDC-backed Pages deploys.

- **Output wiring**
  - Added `github-pages` environment and bound deployment URL to `steps.deployment.outputs.page_url` for native Pages visibility.

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

author: calclavia
body:
## Summary
- allow `createAgentPw()` without `encryptionKey` when the caller only needs profile CRUD
- keep credential and connect APIs fail-fast when `encryptionKey` is missing
- unblock mono `apps/api` profile sync from depending on the Connect encryption secret

## What changed
- make `AgentPwOptions.encryptionKey` optional
- keep `profiles.*` working without an encryption key
- require `AgentPwOptions.encryptionKey` for:
  - `credentials.get`
  - `credentials.list`
  - `credentials.put`
  - `credentials.move`
  - `credentials.delete`
  - `connect.prepare`
  - `connect.startOAuth`
  - `connect.completeOAuth`
- make the low-level OAuth service fail before starting or completing a flow when credential access is unavailable, so web handlers do not create flows that can only fail later

## Why
Mono `apps/api` only syncs generated credential profiles into `agent.pw`; it does not encrypt or decrypt credentials. Requiring the Connect encryption key there is unnecessary secret spread.

This keeps the constructor flexible for profile-only usage without weakening the credential boundary.

### Motivation
- Logs showed most losses come from `outside_lookback` filtering and an overly strict minimum saved-entry threshold that caused the workflow to fail despite successful parsing. 
- The intent is to collect a broader historical set for `youtube-latest.json` while leaving UI-side 24h filtering to the client, and to avoid failing builds for low-but-nonzero saved counts.

- Increased the YouTube collection lookback from `72` to `168` hours by changing the default `lookback_hours` in `helpers/feeds.py` to `168` and adding `YOUTUBE_HISTORY_LOOKBACK_HOURS = 168` in `generate_briefing.py`.

author: copilot
body:
Evolves the minimal single-file bot (one `/start` command, two DB tables) into a full-featured Telegram bot platform covering group management, certified-user lifecycle, subscription enforcement, ratings, coupons, points, risk control, and a web admin dashboard — all deployable on Railway + Postgres.

## Database (`schema.py`)
- 16-table schema auto-initialized on startup via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`
- Tables: `groups`, `settings`, `users`, `certified_users`, `subscription_rules`, `checkins`, `online_status`, `ratings`, `task_definitions`, `user_tasks`, `coupons`, `channel_pushes`, `risk_logs`, `violations`, `verifications`, `points_transactions`
- Thread-safe connection pool extracted to `db.py` (`ThreadedConnectionPool`, `db_exec`/`db_query`/`db_query_one`)

## Bot handlers (`bot/`)
10 aiogram 3.x router modules registered via `bot/__init__.py`:

| Module | Features |
|---|---|
| `group.py` | Math-challenge new-member verification, anti-spam keyword filtering, mute/kick, per-group welcome |
| `subscription.py` | `check_subscriptions(bot, uid, gid, feature)` — checks all required channel memberships before feature access |
| `certified.py` | `/list` (paginated), `/search`, `/user_<id>` — all queries filter `status='active' AND (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > NOW())` |
| `checkin.py` | Daily check-in with streak tracking, points award, `/online`, `/ranking` |
| `nearby.py` | City-based search, online-first sort, smart clarification when no city given |
| `rating.py` | Inline star-rating flow → tag extraction → trust score recalc |
| `coupon.py` | Multi-step FSM publish flow, per-user cooldown, configurable approval |
| `tasks.py` | Daily/weekly/one-time tasks, points ledger, membership upgrades |
| `admin.py` | Full CRUD via FSM, `/freeze`, `/expire`, `/blacklist`, `/push`, `/dashboard` |

## Web admin (`web/routes.py` + `templates/`)
- 25+ FastAPI routes: dashboard, certified-user CRUD, ratings/coupon moderation queues, risk control panel, per-group subscription rule management
- Backward-compatible: existing `/manage` and `/api/set` routes preserved
- 8 Jinja2 templates with Tailwind CSS (dark mode, responsive sidebar)

## Consistency rules applied throughout
- **Expiry**: every public certified-user query enforces `status='active' AND (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > NOW())`
- **Trust score**: `avg_rating × 2 − min(risk_score × 0.1, 2) + min(activity_score × 0.05, 1)`
- **Coupon approval**: CHANNEL_ID presence checked before DB status commit; sets `published` vs `approved` accordingly
- **Admin gate**: checks `ADMIN_IDS` env var first, falls back to `bot.get_chat_member` status

## Environment variables
| Var | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `TOKEN` | Bot token (required) |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres DSN (or `PGHOST`/`PGUSER`/`PGPASSWORD`/`PGDATABASE`) |
| `PUBLISH_CHANNEL_ID` | Channel for auto-push and coupon publishing |
| `ADMIN_IDS` | Comma-separated global admin Telegram UIDs |
| `RAILWAY_STATIC_URL` | Auto-detected for admin dashboard deep-links |

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Implement the CheBot overall platform features in repository `Szchiji/fangzhang`.

CheBot should evolve from a simple certification-user bot into a comprehensive Telegram bot platform with these integrated capabilities:

1. Group management system
- New member verification (captcha/question-based verification)
- Welcome messages
- Anti-spam / anti-ad moderation
- Muting, kicking, permissions, and moderation actions
- Per-group configuration support

2. Multi-group, multi-channel forced subscription
- Allow each group to require subscription to one or more channels
- Allow different bot features to require different subscription sets
- Support user-type-specific rules (normal users, certified users, admins)
- Block feature access until subscriptions are satisfied

3. Certified user management
- CRUD for certified users
- Categories/tags/levels
- Profile pages/cards
- Badges and status labels
- Trust score / credibility score
- Growth score / health score / risk status
- Display certified-user details in bot-friendly format

4. Expiration / lifecycle control
- Custom expiration window for certified users
- Expiration reminders
- Near-expiry de-prioritization
- Expired users must be hidden from user queries
- Expired users cannot speak in group
- Expired users cannot use certified-only actions
- Admins can still inspect historical records

5. Online / check-in system

author: unchidev
body:
## What

Bundle a pre-subsetted Noto Sans CJK JP font (~6.5 MB, OFL-licensed) and
implement Type0/CIDFontType0C composite font embedding so that characters outside
WinAnsiEncoding (CJK ideographs, hiragana, katakana, Greek, Cyrillic, Latin
Extended A/B) render correctly in PDF output.

Closes #1659

## Why

ChordPro files with Japanese titles, lyrics, or artist names produced `?`
placeholders for every non-Latin-1 character.  The root cause was that the
existing `pdf_escape` function is limited to WinAnsiEncoding (U+0000–U+00FF
plus a small 0x80–0x9F extension), and there was no fallback for anything
outside that range.

## How

- **`needs_cid_font(c)`** — routes non-WinAnsiEncoding chars to the CID path.
- **`text_segments(text)`** — splits strings into alternating Latin-1 / CID
  segments so each segment can use the right font.
- **`encode_cid_text`** — converts each char to its 2-byte big-endian GID,
  returning `<GGGG>` hex for PDF `Tj` operators.
- **`PdfDocument::cid_glyphs`** — tracks GID→char pairs for the ToUnicode CMap.
- **`text_at_raw`, `text_at`, `white_text_at`** — split and render each segment
  in its own BT…ET block, switching between `/F1–/F4` (Helvetica) and `/F5`
  (CID font).
- **`build_pdf`** — conditionally emits 5 CID font objects (Type0, CIDFontType0,
  FontDescriptor, FontFile3/CIDFontType0C, ToUnicode CMap) only when non-Latin-1
  glyphs were actually used; ASCII-only PDFs are unchanged.
- **`char_width`** — uses `ttf-parser` advance widths for CID characters so
  layout metrics are correct.

## Known limitation

The bundled font (~6.5 MB) is embedded in full when any non-Latin-1 character
appears.  Per-document glyph subsetting to reduce PDF output size is tracked as
a follow-up.

## Test results

```
test result: ok. 189 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
```

New regression tests:
- `test_cjk_renders_via_cid_font` — verifies CID objects appear and hex GID
  sequences are present for a Japanese-title song.
- `test_mixed_ascii_and_cjk` — verifies both Helvetica and CID fonts appear.
- `test_ascii_only_has_no_cid_font` — verifies CID objects are absent for
  ASCII-only content (no font overhead).

## Sister-site audit

This is a PDF-renderer-only change.  The text and HTML renderers represent
non-ASCII characters as UTF-8 natively and do not need changes.  The WASM, FFI,
and NAPI bindings pass PDF bytes through unchanged — no equivalent fix needed
in sibling crates.

## Review summary

- No security risk: the CID font path uses GID-indexed rendering; there is no
  text interpolation into the PDF stream.
- Dependency addition: `ttf-parser = "0.25"` (read-only font parser, no unsafe
  beyond the standard `unsafe impl Sync` for the parsed `'static` face).
- Font license: `assets/OFL.txt` is included alongside the bundled font.

Final mapping across the Laravel side:
  ROOM_NO   -> room_id   (internal numeric identifier, not shown in UI)
  ROOM_CODE -> room_no   (real classroom code shown to users, e.g. "10018")
  ROOM_DESC -> room_desc (human-readable description)

- room_schedules: add room_id (nullable int) and room_desc (nullable string); change room_no column type from integer to string so codes like "10018" round-trip cleanly.
- attendance_logs: change room_no to string so scanned codes are stored verbatim without integer truncation.
- SyncController::mapRow now reads ROOM_CODE as room_no and ROOM_NO as room_id (with lowercase fallbacks). updateOrCreate persists room_id and room_desc alongside the existing fields.
- RoomScheduleService::getSchedule takes the room code, resolves the internal room_id from stored data, and calls the upstream single-room API with that internal id. findCurrentLecture / forRoom scope take string room codes.
- AttendanceService / ScanController / public RoomScheduleController / Admin\RoomScheduleController / Admin\RoomQrController: room_no is now a string across signatures, validation, and route constraints.
- Admin room-schedules index shows room_code (with small internal id) and a new Room Description column; edit form adds a readonly room_id field and a room_desc input.
- Rooms QR index groups by room_no and shows room_desc under each card; print view shows room_desc beneath the code.
- New en/ar translation keys: rooms.room_id, rooms.room_id_hint, rooms.room_no_hint, rooms.room_desc.

Note: the upstream Node API must emit ROOM_CODE (and ideally ROOM_DESC) in its JSON for the sync to populate these fields. The mapper accepts both uppercase Oracle column names and lowercase fallbacks.

author: christian-sidak
body:
## Summary

- Adds a three-stage fallback to `extract_content_from_html()` so that pages using progressive SSR (hidden pre-hydration markup) are not silently reduced to a single line of loading-shell text
- Stage 1: Readability (existing behavior, unchanged for normal sites)
- Stage 2: readabilipy without Readability JS (less aggressive, does not filter by CSS visibility)
- Stage 3: Raw markdownify conversion (last resort)
- Fallback only activates when Readability output is shorter than 1% of the input HTML

## Motivation

Sites using progressive server-side rendering (Next.js streaming, Remix deferred, custom Lambda SSR) deliver content in two phases: a small visible loading shell, then the real content in a hidden container (`visibility:hidden; position:absolute; top:-9999px`) that becomes visible after client-side hydration. Mozilla Readability treats hidden elements as non-content and strips them entirely, causing `mcp-server-fetch` to return only the loading shell text with no indication that content was lost.

For example, fetching `https://runtimeweb.com` returns just `"Unified Serverless Framework for Full-Stack TypeScript Applications"` instead of the full page content.

## Changes

- `src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py`: Modified `extract_content_from_html()` to try three extraction stages, falling back only when the previous stage produces disproportionately little text
- `src/fetch/tests/test_server.py`: Added 6 unit tests covering all fallback paths, threshold behavior, and no-regression for normal pages

## Breaking Changes

None. The fix only activates when Readability extracts less than 1% of the HTML size as text. Normal sites where Readability works correctly are completely unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] All 6 new fallback tests pass
- [x] Existing tests unaffected (they test Readability directly via Node.js, independent of this change)
- [x] No new dependencies added

Fixes #3878

## Summary
- **Sub-panel schedule matching (Strategy B):** Committees like House Courts of Justice, House Appropriations, House Finance, and House Labor and Commerce have Schedule API entries with hyphen-suffixed sub-panels ("HCJ-Civil", "HCJ-Criminal", "House Appropriations - Health and Human Resources Subcommittee") that carry concrete times while the parent entry has "Time TBA". These sub-panels are NOT in the Committee API (no ParentCommitteeID), so the existing structural lookup never found them. New Strategy B in `find_api_schedule_match` checks for raw name + hyphen/dash prefix matches when Strategy A finds nothing.
- **Map overwrite protection:** `api_schedule_map` no longer overwrites a concrete time with TBA when duplicate entries exist for the same date+committee.

## Root Cause Investigation
Live Schedule API analysis revealed:
- House Courts of Justice: 106 entries, ALL with empty `ScheduleTime`. Times are embedded in Description HTML ("15 minutes after adjournment of House Finance"). Sub-panels "-Civil" and "-Criminal" carry these times.
- 24 fixable date+committee combos across 4 committees: HCJ (11), House Approps (6), House Finance (6), House L&C (1)
- These are the top 4 committees in the "Meeting Actions Missing Times" X-Ray section

## Safety
- Strategy B only fires when Strategy A (structural CHILDREN_OF_PARENT) finds nothing
- Matching uses raw name strings with explicit hyphen check — NOT normalized prefix (which had 505 false positive pairs)
- Overwrite protection preserves existing concrete times, never degrades data quality

author: pazerop
body:
## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive latency tracking for cache operations, enabling detailed performance profiling of the cache system. Latencies are recorded for lock acquisition, local cache operations, remote backend operations, and HTTP communication.

## Key Changes

- **New latency tracking types**: Added `LatencyTracker` (lock-free atomic tracking), `LatencySnapshot` (serializable point-in-time copy), and `LatencyStats` (aggregates for all operation types)
  - Uses atomic compare-and-swap loops for min/max tracking without locks
  - Stores durations in microseconds with sub-microsecond floor to 1µs
  - Provides human-readable formatting (µs/ms/s) via `FormatMs()`

- **Server instrumentation**: Integrated latency recording into `Server.handleGet()` and `Server.handlePut()`:
  - Lock wait time (per-actionID mutex acquisition)
  - Local cache get/put operations
  - Remote backend get operations
  - Remote backend put operations (with semaphore wait tracking)
  - Compression and HTTP request timing in `WebBackend`

- **Concurrency control**: Added `putSem` semaphore (capacity 64) to bound concurrent remote puts, preventing connection churn by reusing pooled HTTP connections

- **HTTP transport tuning**: Enhanced `WebBackend` with optimized `http.Transport` configuration:
  - MaxConnsPerHost: 64 (matches semaphore capacity)
  - MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 64 (keep connections alive)
  - Proper TLS and timeout settings

- **Stats aggregation**: Extended `StatEvent` and `StatsListener` to collect and merge latency snapshots from multiple cache instances

- **CLI output**: Added latency profile display in `cacheprog` showing min/avg/max for each operation type

## Implementation Details

- Latency tracking is optional and only active when `Server.Latency` is populated
- `WebBackend` receives a pointer to `Server.Latency` for sub-operation tracking (compression, HTTP)
- Snapshots are flushed on server close via `flushLatency()` to ensure final stats are captured
- JSON serialization uses compact field names (e.g., "lw" for lock wait) to minimize overhead
- All atomic operations are lock-free to avoid contention during high-throughput scenarios

body:
### Motivation

- Ensure "create from text" places fixtures in the rider-intended left-to-right order when a device type repeats in the same hang instead of forcing symmetric interleaving. 
- Preserve existing per-zone behavior (top/front vs bottom/back and LX sides) while allowing each placement group to independently use symmetric or linear ordering. 
- Place single fixtures centered in the usable hang span to match user expectations instead of pushing them to an edge.

### Description

- Detect repeated fixture type tokens per hang during import and record the hang as requiring linear placement by tracking `seenFixtureTypesByHangInListing` and `linearPlacementHangs` in `core/riderimporter.cpp`.
- Record import order using `importedFixtureOrderByUuid` and `nextImportedFixtureOrder` and add a `buildLinearOrder` function that sorts fixtures by import order for linear placement.
- Switch `placeFixtureGroup` to choose between the existing symmetric ordering (`buildSymmetricOrder`) and the new linear ordering and center a single fixture (`total == 1`) on the usable hang span instead of placing it at an edge, keeping group placement (bottom/top-front/smoke/LX SIDES) unchanged.
- Update text-to-scene documentation in `docs/text_to_scene_rules.md` to describe the new per-hang ordering mode and single-fixture centering behavior.
- Add a regression test and input data: `tests/rider_import_linear_order_test.cpp` and `tests/data/rider_fixture_linear_order.txt`, and register the test in `tests/CMakeLists.txt`.

author: lucasmusikgladjen
body:
## Summary

Two changes — one accessibility fix Codex flagged, one new feature.

### 1. ButtonFieldset accessible names (Codex P2 fix)

The previous restyling collapsed the per-input `<label>` elements into a single outer label wrapping both inputs. A `<label>` only binds to its first nested form control, so the second input ("URL") was effectively unnamed for screen readers and form automation, with only the placeholder as a hint — and placeholders disappear once users type.

**Fix:** the wrapper is now a plain `<div>` and each input gets its own composed `aria-label` (`"Knapp 1 Text"` / `"Knapp 1 URL"`) so assistive tech sees two distinct, persistently-named fields. **Visuals are completely unchanged.**

### 2. Copy-page flow

Adds a small **Kopiera** button that fades in on row hover in the page manager. Clicking opens a dialog with editable `Namn` + `Slug` fields — both optional, defaulting to `<original> COPY` and `<original-slug>-copy` respectively. Submitting POSTs to a new `/api/copy` endpoint and refreshes the list (via a `refreshKey` counter that the existing fetch effect depends on) so the new row appears immediately.

**`/api/copy` handles two flavours:**

- **`type=landing` — deep copy.** Reads the LP record, all linked tabs and all linked downloads, then creates fresh records of each with new linked-record IDs wired up. The new LP owns its own copy of the tabs and downloads, so editing the source afterwards doesn't bleed into the copy.

- **`type=product-area` — shallow copy.** Reads the PA record and creates a new PA with the same field values, including the existing `Products` and `Solutions` linked-record arrays. Airtable links are by reference — multiple PAs already point at shared Products/Solutions in the live base, so deep-copying them would be incorrect.

Both paths reject if the resulting slug already exists (HTTP 409 with a clear error message that the dialog renders inline).

## Test plan

**Accessibility:**
- [ ] Open a product card → inspect a Knapp field's two inputs → each has a distinct `aria-label`

**Copy LP:**
- [ ] Hover an LP row → "Kopiera" button fades in
- [ ] Click → dialog opens with placeholders showing `<name> COPY` and `<slug>-copy`
- [ ] Submit with empty fields → new LP appears in the list with the default name + slug
- [ ] Open the copy → it has the same hero/content/sidebar as the source AND its own tabs (editing them shouldn't affect the source)
- [ ] Try to copy again with the same slug → 409 error rendered inline

**Copy PA:**
- [ ] Hover a PA row → Kopiera button fades in
- [ ] Submit with custom name + slug → new PA appears
- [ ] Open the copy → it shares the same linked Products and Solutions as the source (editing a product affects both pages — expected v1 behaviour)

author: idan-rubin
body:
## Summary
- Agent was fumbling research prompts (e.g. DMV renewal): running 30+ steps after already having the answer, never calling done. Example run: https://browserclaw.org/run/3a675af51cd3498d9da9ab2b699ea678
- Step-16 reasoning literally said *"repeating extraction here is wasteful"* — then did 16 more extractions.
- Root cause: system prompt is gather-biased (scroll ENTIRE page, extract ALL, click every See more), with no symmetric pressure to submit. `shouldBlockDone` blocks done but nothing forces it.

## Changes
- **System prompt**: replaced the old "Before calling done" checklist with a "When to call done" rule that makes `done` mandatory once memory contains enough to answer — even partially.
- **Periodic answer-readiness check**: every 6 steps after step 8, a cheap LLM call judges whether current memory already supports an answer. If yes, `forceComplete` with the accumulated data.
- **MAX_STEPS now returns success** when we gathered useful data, with the summary as the answer — instead of `success: false` + "hit step limit". Hitting the cap with a partial answer is still a win for the user.
- **getFinalSummary prompt** rewritten — it's a wrap-up, not a "stopped due to repeated failures" report.
- **Crash logging fix**: `session-manager.ts` was swallowing the error object in the crash log. Now includes `err` + `message` so we can actually diagnose prod crashes.

Three independent terminators now: the model itself (new prompt), readiness check (every 6 steps), max-step backstop (success + partial).

## Test plan
- [ ] `npm run lint` / `tsc` / `npm test` / `npm run build` — all green locally (156 tests pass)
- [ ] Deploy to prod and re-run the DMV renewal prompt — expect done by step ~12 with a structured answer
- [ ] Re-run other sample prompts — confirm they complete instead of running to step cap
- [ ] Check prod logs after next crash — verify the error object is now visible

author: copilot
body:
Adds PyInstaller-based packaging to produce self-contained `social-sync` binaries for macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64), eliminating the Python/pip requirement for end users.

### Core changes

- **`sync.spec`** — PyInstaller spec producing a single-file `social-sync` executable; bundles `src/`, `.env.example`, and explicit hidden imports for atproto, mastodon.py, pydantic-settings, cryptography, etc. UPX disabled to avoid macOS code-signing conflicts.
- **`pyproject.toml` / `requirements-dev.txt`** — Added `pyinstaller>=6.0.0` to dev dependencies.
- **`.gitignore`** — Added `!sync.spec` negation to override the blanket `*.spec` exclusion.

### CI/CD

- **`.github/workflows/build-binaries.yml`** — Triggers on version tags (`[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+`) and `workflow_dispatch`. Matrix builds across `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-13`, `macos-14`; verifies each binary with `--help`/`--version`; attaches all three to the GitHub Release via `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`. Build jobs use `contents: read`, release job uses `contents: write`.

### Documentation

- **`README.md`** — Added "Download Standalone Binary" section with platform-specific `curl -fL` one-liners and a binary-first usage section.
- **`docs/CHANGELOG.md`** — Entry under `[Unreleased] > Added`.

### Build locally

```bash
pip install pyinstaller>=6.0.0
pyinstaller sync.spec --clean --noconfirm
./dist/social-sync --help
```

body:
### Motivation

- Move from a single deterministic projection to a reusable stochastic engine so the app can present probabilities and realistic outcome ranges. 
- Provide a clear, low-friction integration path to surface Monte Carlo results first in `RetirementResultView` and later in `AdjustmentExplorerView`.

### Description

- Add a standalone simulation core at `MyRetire/MonteCarloSimulator.swift` that defines `MonteCarloSimulator` with `Inputs` and `Results`, a `run(_:)` method, normal-return sampling via a Box–Muller generator, and percentile extraction. 
- The simulator uses sensible defaults such as a minimum of `250` trials and a volatility floor, and handles the zero-years edge case by returning the current savings as the outcome. 
- Add `docs/monte-carlo-integration-plan.md` that documents recommended placement (use `ProfileData` for inputs), first UI surface (`RetirementResultView`), next step (`AdjustmentExplorerView`), and suggested assumptions (per-mix volatility and recommended trial counts).

### Testing

- No automated unit tests were added or executed for this change; the change is limited to adding a reusable model file and documentation and is ready for unit test coverage and UI integration in follow-up work.

author: aupv9
body:
## Summary

- **RS256 token signing** — new `internal/crypto.KeyManager` generates an RSA-2048 key pair at startup (persisted to disk when `jwt.rsa_key_path` is set). All access tokens and ID tokens are now signed with RS256; HS256 is accepted as a fallback for backward compatibility during rollout.
- **Proper JWKS endpoint** — `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` now returns the real RSA public key JWK (`kty=RSA`, `alg=RS256`, `n`, `e`, `kid`). In HS256 mode the key set is intentionally empty (the shared secret is never published over the network).
- **OIDC discovery updated** — `idTokenSigningAlgValuesSupported` now reflects the active algorithm (`RS256` or `HS256`).
- **RBAC scope middleware** — new `middleware.RequireScope(...scopes)` checks that the JWT `scope` claim contains at least one of the required scopes (HTTP 403 on failure). `RequireAuth` is extended to cache parsed `jwt_claims` in gin context so downstream middleware can read them without re-parsing.
- **`RequirePermission` stub** — `middleware.RequirePermission(checker, resource, action)` delegates to `PermissionChecker.HasPermission`; when `checker` is nil the middleware is a no-op, so routes can be registered before the Phase-2 RBAC data layer is merged.
- **UserInfo tenant extraction fix** — `HandleUserInfo` now extracts `tenant_id` directly from the Bearer token claims when `TenantContext` middleware could not resolve a tenant from the request headers, eliminating the previous "return 401 immediately" dead code.
- **Introspection scope fix** — the JWT fallback path in `IntrospectToken` now returns `claims.Scope` (was hardcoded to `""`).
- **Config hardening** — removed two `fmt.Printf("DEBUG: …")` statements that leaked `DATABASE_URL` to stdout on every startup; added `jwt.algorithm` and `jwt.rsa_key_path` config fields.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` — no compilation errors
- [x] `go vet ./...` — no issues
- [x] `go test ./...` — all 6 packages green (including 6 new crypto tests + 12 new RBAC middleware tests)
- [ ] Start server (`make start`), confirm `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` returns `kty=RSA` with `n` and `e` fields
- [ ] Confirm `GET /.well-known/openid-configuration` reports `"RS256"` in `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`
- [ ] Issue a token, decode the JWT header — `alg` must be `RS256` and `kid` must match the JWKS entry
- [ ] Call `POST /oauth/introspect` with a valid token — `scope` must be present in response
- [ ] Call `GET /userinfo` without `X-Tenant-ID` header but with a valid Bearer token — must return 200 (not 401)
- [ ] Verify no `DEBUG:` lines appear in server logs on startup

author: copilot
body:
# Pull request

## Closes

## 📑 Description

Concurrent `opencode` runs on the same branch were racing to push branch updates, causing rejected pushes when one run advanced remote state first.  
This change introduces branch/PR-scoped workflow concurrency so only one OpenCode run executes per context at a time.

- **Workflow concurrency guard**
  - Added top-level `concurrency` to `.github/workflows/opencode.yml`.
  - Configured `cancel-in-progress: false` to queue later runs instead of terminating active work.

- **Context-aware grouping**
  - Group key now scopes by workflow + PR/issue/branch context:
    - `pull_request.number` when present
    - fallback to `issue.number`, `head_ref`, then `ref_name`

- **Workflow catalog sync**
  - Updated `.github/workflows/AGENTS.md` to document the new OpenCode concurrency behavior.

```yaml
concurrency:
  cancel-in-progress: false
  group: >-
    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
```

## ✅ Checks
- [x] My pull request follows the code style of this project
- [x] I have updated the documentation as required, or no documentation updates are needed
- [x] All required tests and checks have passed

## ℹ Additional Information

Scope is intentionally limited to `opencode.yml`; `opencode-review.yml` behavior is unchanged.
